name: Advergent Lead Scoring System V2
description: B2B companies that can benefit from paid acquisition funnels. Prioritizes signals we can reliably detect (vertical fit, sales model, traction) over hidden signals (exact pricing).
target_verticals: Service providers wanting paid acquisition channel

vertical_fit.description: Does this company fit our target verticals?

scoring_guide.10: B2B SaaS selling to businesses, Agency/Consultancy with high-ticket services, Coach/Program with premium offers
scoring_guide.8: Vertical SaaS (niche industry software), Professional services firm, MarTech/RevTech tools
scoring_guide.6: B2B but unclear offer structure, Marketplace with B2B component
scoring_guide.4: Mixed B2B/B2C model, B2B but very early stage
scoring_guide.2: Primarily B2C with some B2B, Dev tools sold to engineers (not business buyers)
scoring_guide.0: Pure B2C, Consumer app, E-commerce product brand, Infrastructure/developer tools only

sales_model.description: Do they sell via demos/calls (not self-serve)?

scoring_guide.10: Explicit 'Book a Demo' / 'Talk to Sales' / 'Get a Quote' as primary CTA, No visible pricing (implies custom/enterprise)
scoring_guide.8: Demo CTA present alongside self-serve option, 'Contact Us' for enterprise tier
scoring_guide.6: Hybrid model: self-serve entry + sales-assisted upsell, Free trial that leads to sales conversation
scoring_guide.4: Primarily self-serve with optional demo, Pricing fully visible but has 'Enterprise: Contact Us'
scoring_guide.2: Fully self-serve, all pricing visible, no sales involvement
scoring_guide.0: No clear sales process, Product-led only with no human touchpoint

traction.description: Do they have proof of real business traction?

scoring_guide.10: Named enterprise customers (Fortune 500, recognizable logos), Funding disclosed ($5M+), Revenue/growth metrics shared, 1000+ customers claimed
scoring_guide.8: Good customer logos visible, Customer testimonials with titles/companies, Case studies with results, 100+ customers or strong social proof
scoring_guide.6: Some testimonials present, LinkedIn shows 50+ employees, Has been in business 2+ years, Some press/media mentions
scoring_guide.4: Limited social proof, Small team (10-50 employees), Early but has some customers, Seed funded or bootstrapped with revenue
scoring_guide.2: Very early stage, Few/no testimonials, Team <10 people, Recently launched
scoring_guide.0: No visible traction, Looks like a landing page only, Pre-revenue/pre-launch

buyer_reachability.description: Can we reach the decision-maker via Meta/LinkedIn ads?

scoring_guide.10: Buyer is founder/CEO/business owner (very active on social), Target is marketers, sales leaders, or growth roles (native to paid channels)
scoring_guide.8: Buyer is VP/Director level in non-technical function (Operations, Finance, HR), SMB owners who are on Facebook/LinkedIn
scoring_guide.6: Buyer is mid-market executive, May use LinkedIn but less active, Mixed technical/business buyer
scoring_guide.4: Buyer is technical (CTO, Engineering Manager) but at business-focused company, Enterprise buyer who uses LinkedIn professionally
scoring_guide.2: Buyer is developer/engineer who doesn't engage with ads, Highly technical audience (DevOps, Data Engineers)
scoring_guide.0: Buyer is procurement/committee (enterprise RFP process), Pure developer audience, Government/institutional buyer

offer_price.description: Is this likely a high-ticket offer ($3K+)?

scoring_guide.10: Explicit high-ticket pricing visible ($5K+/deal or $1K+/month), 'Starting at $X,000', Enterprise-only positioning
scoring_guide.8: No pricing visible + demo-based sales model (strong signal of high-ticket), Custom pricing / 'Get a Quote'
scoring_guide.7: No pricing visible + B2B SaaS in target vertical (benefit of doubt), Agency/consultancy (typically high-ticket)
scoring_guide.5: Pricing visible in $500-3K range, Mid-market positioning
scoring_guide.3: Pricing visible in $100-500/month range, SMB-focused with lower ACVs

disqualifiers.name: pure_b2c
disqualifiers.description: Pure B2C - Consumer product with no B2B component

disqualifiers.name: toxic_reputation
disqualifiers.description: Toxic reputation - Significant negative reviews indicating scam/fraud patterns

disqualifiers.name: pure_devtools
disqualifiers.description: Pure infrastructure/dev tools - Buyer is exclusively developers finding tools through GitHub/HackerNews

disqualifiers.name: pre_revenue_no_funding
disqualifiers.description: Pre-revenue with no funding - No customers AND no funding AND less than 6 months old

disqualifiers.name: enterprise_long_cycle
disqualifiers.description: Enterprise-only with 12+ month sales cycles - Government, healthcare systems, Fortune 100 procurement

disqualifiers.name: direct_competitor
disqualifiers.description: Direct competitor - Offers same service as Advergent (paid ads agency)
